comparison: Perfect agreement on baseline characteristics (C25-C32, C92-C96). Both evaluations find the demographic and molecular characteristics appropriately reported and supported. OpenEval notes internal consistency; peer reviewers affirm the trial design was 'meticulously structured.'

Strong agreement on efficacy outcomes (C33-C43). Both find the response rates and disease control rate well-supported. OpenEval validates the DCR calculation; peer reviewers explicitly affirm the 'high disease control rate' and note the trial design was rigorous. Peer review also addresses C44, C46, C76, C90 which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Both address survival outcomes (C44, C46), finding them supported despite historical control limitations. OpenEval notes statistical significance with appropriate caveats about non-randomized comparison. Peer reviewers affirm the findings as part of overall efficacy assessment.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty of subgroup analyses (C47-C50). Both evaluations acknowledge the numerical trends lack statistical significance due to limited sample size. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN; peer reviewers present as exploratory findings requiring larger studies.

Perfect agreement on abscopal effect (C51-C52). Both find the imaging data supporting regression in target and off-target lesions. OpenEval notes the mechanism is inferred; peer reviewers explicitly endorse the finding and note it underscores radiation therapy's potential to enhance immunotherapy.

Perfect agreement on safety profile (C53-C55, C77). Both evaluations find the adverse event data comprehensive and favorable. OpenEval notes consistency with known toxicities; peer reviewers affirm the safety profile is 'crucial for patients who have already undergone multiple lines of therapy.'

Strong agreement on transcriptome and immunohistochemistry findings (C56-C61, C63). Both find the methods appropriate and data well-supported. OpenEval validates NanoString and DESeq2 approaches; peer reviewers initially requested methodological details but confirmed after revision that analyses were appropriate and conclusions supported.

Perfect agreement on NOS2 upregulation finding (C62). Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval notes the interpretation requires further validation; peer reviewers implicitly accept it as part of comprehensive gene expression analysis without specific challenge.

Strong agreement on pathway analyses (C64-C70). Both find gene set enrichment and pathway analyses well-supported. OpenEval validates the methods and figures; peer reviewers confirm bioinformatics approaches were appropriate and supplementary data corroborate conclusions.

Strong agreement on tumor microenvironment changes (C71-C74). Both find reductions in immunosuppressive populations and favorable microenvironment changes well-supported. OpenEval validates mechanistic insights; peer reviewers affirm 'significant improvements in the tumor's immune landscape' and accepted mechanistic explanations after revision. Peer review also addresses C84, C91.

Perfect agreement on negative findings in non-responders (C75). Both evaluations support this as valid negative finding. OpenEval notes it strengthens mechanistic interpretation; peer reviewers state this 'does not undermine the overall integrity' and supports specificity of treatment effects.

Agreement on main conclusions (C76, C84-C87, C90-C91). OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported by clinical and mechanistic data integration. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the study 'offers a safe and powerful later-line option' and results are supported. Partial overlap with peer R1 and R5.

Perfect agreement on study limitations (C88-C89). Both evaluations find the authors appropriately acknowledge small sample size and single-arm design limitations. OpenEval notes these limit generalizability; peer reviewers initially requested discussion of limitations and confirmed authors adequately addressed them in revision.

Perfect agreement on methodology (C97-C109). Both find methods appropriate and well-established. OpenEval validates RECIST criteria, NanoString, and statistical methods; peer reviewers initially requested more methodological details but confirmed after revision that methods were satisfactory and appropriate.

OpenEval evaluated background and rationale claims (C1-C24, C78-C83) as supported by appropriate citations and established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background claims.
